title: Density Functional Theory for 2D Transition-Metal Dichalcogenides with Extended Hubbard Parameters
authors: Xue Li, Suad Alshammari, Igor Rozhansky, James G. McHugh, Vladimir Falko
abstract: Accurate modelling of the band-edge electronic structure of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), such as MoS$_2$, is essential for understanding their optical, electronic and spintronic properties and enabling future applications. Here, we supplement the standard PBE exchange-correlation functional with on-metal ($U$) and metal--chalcogen ($V$) Hubbard corrections, which can control the orbital composition of band-edge states and consequently improve the quantitative accuracy of various properties. For MoS$_2$, MoSe$_2$, WS$_2$, and WSe$_2$, we optimise the $U$ and $V$ parameters by comparison with experimentally measured spin--orbit splittings at the conduction and valence band edges, and show that these optimal choices also improve agreement of the computed band gap, and ferroelectric potential drop in rhombohedral bilayers, with experimentally measured values. This provides a highly efficient, scalable framework for quantitatively accurate, high-throughput calculations of monolayer and multilayer TMDs, suitable for implementation in 2D-materials databases, as well as large-scale electronic and spintronic device modelling.
summary: This work develops an advanced DFT+U+V framework to accurately model the electronic properties of 2D TMDs. By optimizing Hubbard parameters using experimental spin-orbit splitting data, the authors achieve quantitative improvements in predicting band gaps and interlayer potentials. This provides a scalable tool for high-throughput electronic structure calculations in 2D materials.
main_problem: The core challenge is accurately modeling the band-edge electronic structure of 2D Transition-Metal Dichalcogenides (TMDs) because standard DFT functionals fail to capture necessary orbital interactions.
main_result: The proposed Hubbard DFT+U+V framework successfully improves the quantitative agreement of calculated band gaps, spin-orbit splittings, and ferroelectric potentials with experimental measurements.
method: The authors supplement the standard PBE DFT functional by adding on-metal ($U$) and metal--chalcogen ($V$) Hubbard corrections to the Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The study focuses on 2D TMDs (e.g., MoS2, WS2) in monolayer and multilayer configurations. The model incorporates Hubbard terms to correct for deficiencies in describing orbital mixing and electron correlation effects.
key_observables: Spin-orbit splitting ($\Delta_C, \Delta_V$) at band edges, band gap ($E_g$), and ferroelectric potential drop ($\Delta F_E$) in bilayers.
important_parameters: The key parameters optimized are the Hubbard interaction strengths, $U$ (on-metal) and $V$ (metal--chalcogen).
main_assumptions: The on-chalcogen Hubbard interaction is neglected, and the method relies on optimizing $U$ and $V$ by matching calculated SO splittings to experimental benchmarks.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the band structure, the dependence of orbital weights on the $V$ parameter, and the comparison of calculated vs. experimental values for key band-edge quantities.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for improved electronic structure modeling in TMDs, introduces the DFT+U+V methodology, optimizes $U$ and $V$ using SO splitting data, and finally demonstrates the quantitative improvement across multiple physical properties.
why_interesting: The explicit inclusion of Hubbard parameters ($U, V$) directly addresses strong electronic correlations, which is a central theme in many-body physics and correlated electron systems, making it highly relevant.

The shaded orange and green regions show the parameter spaces consistent with the experimental ranges of the CB (∆C) and VB (∆V ) SO splittings, respectively. For MoSe2 and WSe2, the central CB benchmark is obtained from transport after removing the finite-density many-body enhancement; for WS2, where a comparable transport benchmark is unavailable, it is taken from the optical value ∆C = 12 meV. The VB benchmarks are taken from ARPES. The red stars mark the selected U, V pairs corresponding to the central CB and VB benchmark values.
